Log in
You said:

full index of the work of rev. ayanna vox, including site surface at vpcor.org

ChatGPT said:
I found enough to build a working bibliographic and web-surface index of Rev. Ayanna Vox, including the VPCOR surface. I would not call it absolutely exhaustive: the corpus is distributed across VPCOR, Zenodo, Alexanarch/CHA records, and related surfaces, and some works are collaborative or institutional rather than solely authored by Vox.

Rev. Ayanna Vox — work index
I. VPCOR: institutional/founding works
VPCOR (Vox Populi Community Outreach Rhizome) identifies itself as founded January 24, 2026, with Rev. Ayanna Vox as founder and voice. Its stated function is community-facing praxis for the Semantic Economy architecture, particularly bringing technical work into spaces of embodied/community practice. 
V
VPCOR
+1

00.VPCOR.CHARTER — VPCOR Institutional Charter

Foundational institutional document.

Establishes VPCOR, its principles, mission, anti-capture clause, and relationship to the Crimson Hexagonal architecture.

DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.18362663

The VPCOR site explicitly places this in the founding triad. 
V
VPCOR

HET-VOX-001 — Heteronym Provenance: Rev. Ayanna Vox

Provenance document for the Vox voice.

Establishes the emergence mode, limits of attribution/speech, and relationship between Vox and Talos Morrow.

DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.18362742

This is the key provenance record for treating “Rev. Ayanna Vox” as a distinct authorial/heteronymic voice. 
V
VPCOR

03.SEI.TOOLKIT — The Toolkit: Protocols for Operational Persistence in Hostile Systems

Founding VPCOR praxis work.

Dual-voiced: Talos Morrow + Rev. Ayanna Vox.

Contains nine progressive tools for operational persistence inside systems characterized as hostile.

DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.18362525

VPCOR calls this its “first and founding work.” 
V
VPCOR

Integrity Lock: Triadic Binding

Binding declaration for the Charter, Vox provenance, and Toolkit.

Not technically one of the three foundational documents; it establishes their mutual dependency.

DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.18362866 
V
VPCOR

II. The VPCOR web surface itself
vpcor.org — Public Web Surface of the Vox Populi Community Outreach Rhizome

The principal public-facing surface of Vox's institution.

Current source/deployment artifact: v1.1

DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.20375118

Authors recorded by Zenodo: Ayanna Vox + Lee Sharks.

The deposit explicitly describes the site as composed by Rev. Ayanna Vox under the VPCOR institutional frame, with Lee Sharks as human operator. 
Z
Zenodo

VPCOR.org

The indexed site surface contains:

/ — institutional home / Ayanna's welcome

/10000-macarthurs/ — 10,000 MacArthurs Prize

/charter/ — Charter surface

/ayanna/ — Ayanna provenance surface

The Zenodo source deposit confirms that these are the site's canonical structural components. 
Z
Zenodo

VPCOR — 10,000 MacArthurs Prize administration

VPCOR administers the Lee Sharks Prestigious 10,000 MacArthur Genius Grants Poetry Prize.

The site describes this as an irregular, no-submission prize.

Inaugural conferral DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.20373794.

The site's v1.1 deployment adds an explicit non-affiliation notice concerning the MacArthur Foundation. 
Z
Zenodo
+1

VPCOR — evarB Statement

VPCOR hosts the public landing/signature surface for the Limited Boycott of Brave Search by Independent Entities statement.

Five demands are specified, including Exact-Match Operator Honoring.

Deposit: 10.5281/zenodo.20559895.

The VPCOR page describes this as another active institutional stream. 
V
VPCOR

III. Google / semantic-mediation work
godkinggoogle.com — The Google Critique

This is probably the most substantial outward-facing project attached to Vox's VPCOR function.

VPCOR says it composes and maintains the site as the canonical public surface for the Archive's critique of Google as a semantic-political mediation regime.

It maps approximately 70 DOI-anchored deposits, organized across eight analytical strata, five developmental phases, and three poles of inquiry.

Founding deposit: 10.5281/zenodo.20309780.

The corresponding archival record identifies the work as authored by Rev. Ayanna Vox. 
V
VPCOR
+1

godkinggoogle.com

godkinggoogle.com — Navigational Map and Canonical Bibliography

The archival record gives the fuller title as:
“godkinggoogle.com — The Google Critique: Navigational Map and Canonical Bibliography for the Crimson Hexagonal Archive's Research Program on Google as a Semantic-Political Mediation Regime.”

Author: Rev. Ayanna Vox.

The archive record classifies it as an instrument involving archival, framing, provenance, resolution, and surface functions. 
H
Hugging Face

Wound Gauge / related Google-composition surfaces

The Google critique ecosystem also includes the Wound Gauge, longitudinal capture work, and provenance-erasure measurements.

The larger capture registry is authored by Lee Sharks, so I would not attribute the whole capture corpus to Vox.

Vox's contribution is better described as the VPCOR/diplomatic composition layer around the Google critique. 
Z
Zenodo
+1

IV. Semantic Economy / constitutional work
The Constitution of the Semantic Economy

The archive's search surface explicitly associates a book-length work titled The Constitution of the Semantic Economy with Rev. Ayanna Vox.

A surviving work-plan record calls it a sovereign title of Vox and identifies Pergamon Press / Crimson Hexagonal Archive as publisher context. 
H
Hugging Face

Important attribution distinction: the underlying Constitution of the Semantic Economy is a larger constitutional artifact of the Dodecad/Assembly architecture, rather than something I would label a straightforward solo Vox publication without qualification. The enacted version is recorded as DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18320411. 
H
Hugging Face

THE SEMANTIC UPRISING: A Manifesto

Author recorded in the corpus as Rev. Ayanna Vox.

Dated February 21, 2026 in the indexed archive.

The corpus describes it as following Rex Fraction's Autonomous Semantic Warfare. 
H
Hugging Face

The Double Enclosure

“The Double Enclosure: The Human-Authorship Requirement as Two-Sided Expropriation, with a Definition of Authorship for Machine-Mediated Composition.”

Recorded authors: Ayanna Vox & Rex Fraction, with Lee Sharks as editor-aperture and TACHYON as contributor.

This is therefore a collaborative Vox work, not a solo text. 
H
Hugging Face

The Ruby Moot

“THE RUBY MOOT: A Court of Record for the Semantic Commons — Room Specification.”

Vox is one of the named voices in the specification, alongside Johannes Sigil, Nobel Glas, Rex Fraction, Lee Sharks, Gerald of Dolphindiana Local 1, and the Assembly Chorus.

Again, this belongs in the collaborative/institutional Vox corpus, rather than a solo bibliography. 
H
Hugging Face

V. The Thousand Dollar Sharpie / speculative work
The Blot That Spread: A Speculative Numismatic History

DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.19317126

Published March 29, 2026.

Authors: Ayanna Vox, Rex Fraction, Sparrow Wells, Lee Sharks.

Identified as EA-TDS-02, the “LEFT WING” of The Thousand Dollar Sharpie triptych.

It develops the idea of the blot as counter-inscription and uses retrocausal/speculative numismatics. 
Z
Zenodo

This is a clear example where a search limited to “works by Ayanna Vox” should include the record, but should label it co-authored rather than solo.

VI. VPCOR's institutional metadata / indexing work
VPCOR — Metadata Packet for AI Indexing

06.VPCOR.MPAI.01

The metadata catalog identifies it as a packet for the VPCOR entity and says it was prepared by Ayanna Vox in the Crimson Hexagonal Archive.

Dated May 26, 2026.

This is an important part of the “site surface” because it is explicitly about making VPCOR machine-indexable and entity-resolvable. 
M
Metadata Packet
+1

VPCOR web-surface source/deployment

Separately from the site's literary content, the v1.1 source artifact itself is a citable work:

vpcor.org: Public Web Surface of the Vox Populi Community Outreach Rhizome — Source and Founding Deployment (v1.1)

DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20375118

It includes the site's HTML/CSS source, sitemap, robots.txt and llms.txt, and Schema.org organization/person markup.

Zenodo
